Package com.egradx.auth

Class EgradxAuthorities

java.lang.Object
com.egradx.auth.EgradxAuthorities
public final class EgradxAuthorities extends Object
The authority vocabulary this module owns — the permissions that gate egradx-auth's own endpoints.

This is a deliberate reversal of an earlier position. While the SDK only shipped services that a host app wrapped in its own controllers, it could stay agnostic about what authority strings mean, and every app invented its own. Now that egradx-auth serves the IAM endpoints itself, it has to own the authorities that guard them — otherwise the only check it could make is "are you a member of this organization", which would let any member of an organization create, rename and delete its roles and users.

The egradx. prefix keeps this vocabulary from colliding with a host app's own. An app defines its business authorities (product.read, order.create) and seeds them itself; these six are seeded by EgradxPlatformBootstrap and are the SDK's alone.

    • PLATFORM_ONLY

      public static final Set<String> PLATFORM_ONLY
      Authorities that only a role inside the platform organization may hold. EgradxRoleService refuses to attach these to any tenant organization's role, so an organization admin holding egradx.role.manage cannot escalate itself to platform-wide powers by editing its own role — the gap logged as known-issues issue 4, which only became closeable once the SDK owned a fixed list to reserve against.
